notes.source: multi-agent Labyrinth formation pass (Workflow tool, one agent per subsystem node), independently spot-checked before commit
key_findings: docs/ is the mkdocs-material human-facing documentation source (mkdocs.yml, docs_dir: docs), published to https://jaxfne.readthedocs.io/. Verified live: `mkdocs build --strict` succeeds cleanly (1.80s, zero warnings/errors) on the current dev-branch tree.

Scale (via `find docs -type f`, ~140 files): api/ (13 pages), guides/ (18), tutorials/ (24, incl. versioned + 'Suite No.' variants + a legacy tutorials_v030/ tree with its own figures/manifests/reports), releases/ (7 version-pinned pages), notes/ (2), _static/tutorial_figures/ (12 PNGs + figure_manifest.json), assets/ (interactive HTML explorers + PNG showcases), _generated/ (operator_inventory.md, version.md), plus top-level pages (index.md, quickstart.md, changelog.md, scope_and_status.md, for_ai_agents.md, ci_policy.md, faq.md, migration_guide.md, etc).

docs/for_ai_agents.md (lines ~3-10) documents a deliberate three-surface split: docs/+README = humans (tutorials/API/guides); skills/+AGENTS.md = AI agents (verified workflows/API catalog, same source-of-truth as the package, not a parallel spec); artifacts/developer/ = maintainers/agents, local-only and gitignored since 2026-07-14 (absent from a fresh clone).

docs/_generated/version.md is machine-written by scripts/sync_docs_version.py (regex-reads pyproject.toml's [project].version) + scripts/sync_release_metadata.py, and is intentionally excluded from mkdocs nav via mkdocs.yml's `exclude_docs:` block (mkdocs.yml lines ~11-16) — this is a documented, deliberate exclusion, not an accidental orphan.

scripts/check_docs_orphans.py is a CI-only hard gate (not part of mkdocs itself) that fails if any docs/*.md file isn't reachable from mkdocs.yml's nav tree — it exists because `mkdocs build --strict` treats orphan pages as cosmetic INFO only, not a failure; added after 16 pages were once silently orphaned from nav (regression fixed 2026-07-08).

docs/ci_policy.md documents the real two-tier CI split relevant to docs changes: fast CI (ci.yml) runs on every push (compileall, ~2759 pytest tests minus two --ignored files and slow-marked tests, examples/00-08, wheel+sdist build, smoke test); release_ci.yml runs the full matrix + slow tests on main/nightly. Notebook execution (28 release-facing notebooks) is handled by a separate notebook_execution.yml workflow, not ci.yml.

skills/jaxfne-notebook-release-gate/SKILL.md is the operative skill for this subsystem — it explicitly covers notebook/tutorial/docs/manifest/release validation and its checklist includes running `mkdocs build --strict` (SKILL.md line ~84) before declaring a docs/release task done.

FRICTIONS_STACK.md F-027 (closed 2026-07-13) is the one directly-relevant historical incident: a stale canonical-column cell-type-fraction table (≈77E:23I, 'PV absent in L1') had propagated from jaxfne/builders.py's docstring into 5 docs/ files — docs/quickstart.md, docs/api/index.md, docs/guides/configuration_grammar.md, docs/tutorials/07_jaxfne_suite_no_2_spectrolaminar_motif.md, and docs/tutorials/13_canonical_column_etude.md (table + worked example + prose + a plot title). Real figures are ≈66E:34I overall, PV peaks at L2/L3 (25% each), absent at L6 not L1 — fixed at the source (builders.py) and in all 5 docs pages plus the skill. This demonstrates docs/ numeric claims can silently drift from the live `jtfne.CANONICAL_LAYER_CELL_TYPE_FRACTIONS` constant and must be spot-checked against a fresh `construct(cfg).neuron_table()` run, not trusted at face value.

AGENTS.md § 'Skills sync' and docs/for_ai_agents.md both note: repo skills mirror to global agent installs via `bash skills/SYNC_GLOBAL.sh` — relevant if a docs task also touches a skill's SKILL.md content that references docs/ pages, since skill edits need syncing separately from docs edits (docs/ itself has no sync step, it's committed directly).
contracts: mkdocs.yml is the single nav/build contract: any new docs/*.md page must be added to its `nav:` tree or scripts/check_docs_orphans.py will fail CI (this is enforced independently of mkdocs's own --strict, which only WARNs on orphans).

docs/_generated/version.md and mkdocs.yml's jaxfne_version extra field are machine-owned by scripts/sync_docs_version.py — should be regenerated via that script after a version bump, not hand-edited (mkdocs.yml's own comment at line ~11-14 states this explicitly).

docs/requirements.txt pins the doc-build toolchain: mkdocs>=1.6.1, mkdocs-material>=9.7.6, pymdown-extensions>=11.0.1 — the versions actually used for the successful --strict build verified in this session.

docs/for_ai_agents.md formally designates itself + skills/ + AGENTS.md as the AI-agent-facing surface, and docs/+README as the human surface — a docs/ page's job is human tutorials/guides/API reference, not agent workflow instructions (per AGENTS.md line ~59-61: 'Don't copy "language: prefer X avoid Y" phrasing ... into docs/ or README').

Interactive visualization assets under docs/assets/interactive/*.html and docs/assets/showcases/*.html are checked in as static pre-rendered artifacts (e.g. izhikevich_single_emitter_explorer.html, v037_source_column_3d.html) alongside a manifest.json — not generated at mkdocs build time.
landmines: Numeric/prose claims in docs/ (config defaults, cell-type fractions, layer breakdowns) drift silently from the live package and are NOT caught by `mkdocs build --strict` (which only checks link/nav/config validity, not factual accuracy) — FRICTIONS_STACK F-027 found a stale canonical-column table propagated into 5 docs/ pages before being caught by an external review, not by CI. Any docs/ edit touching a numeric claim should be spot-checked against a fresh live run, not copied from an existing doc.

Orphaned docs pages (a .md file that exists but isn't linked from mkdocs.yml nav) do NOT fail `mkdocs build --strict` — only scripts/check_docs_orphans.py catches this, and only if it's actually wired into CI; don't rely on `mkdocs build --strict` alone as the completeness gate for a new page.

docs/_generated/version.md must stay excluded from mkdocs nav (mkdocs.yml `exclude_docs:`) — adding it to nav would make mkdocs treat a machine-written sync target as a human-navigable page, defeating its purpose; this exclusion is deliberate, don't 'fix' it by removing the exclude_docs entry.

This session ran `mkdocs build --strict`, which created/overwrote a `site/` directory in the repo root as a build artifact. It is not tracked by git (confirmed via `git status --short`, not listed) but a fresh agent running the same build command will do the same — clean it up if it matters, don't assume it's gitignored without checking (not verified against .gitignore contents in this pass).
